title: Champlain from Quebec to Lake Champlain and Huronia, 1608–15
summary: Champlain founded Quebec in 1608 as a trading post and bound France to the Innu, Algonquin and Huron-Wendat. In 1609 he went up the Richelieu to the lake that now has his name with an Algonquin and Huron war party, and his musket killed two Mohawk chiefs. In 1615 he went up the Ottawa River and by Lake Nipissing to Georgian Bay, among the Huron-Wendat, and on with them to attack an Onondaga fort.

events.label: Quebec founded
events.text: A habitation of three buildings at the narrows, beside the old site of Stadacona. Scurvy killed most of the first winter's men.

events.label: The Mohawk skirmish on Lake Champlain
events.doubt: The site is put near Ticonderoga or Crown Point.
events.text: Champlain and two other Frenchmen with an Algonquin, Innu and Huron war party met Mohawk on the lake. A shot from his arquebus killed two chiefs, and the Mohawk fled. The fighting began a long enmity between New France and the Iroquois.

events.label: Huronia: among the Huron-Wendat
events.text: He reached the villages of Wendake on Georgian Bay, and wintered there with the Huron-Wendat. Étienne Brûlé, his interpreter, had gone there before him.
